name: pixel-image

frames.best_why: Every tile is in and the sunset colour has fully replaced greyscale: the finished state.

tagline: A photo assembles from scattered square tiles, then colour bleeds in.
summary: Splits an image into a grid of tiles that fade in one at a time at random, starting grey and then washing into full colour after a pause.
appearance: A rounded square photo of snowy peaks above a sea of cloud is centred on black. While it assembles it reads as a patchwork of square tiles with black gaps; settled, it is one unbroken picture with soft sunset pinks and blues.
behaviour: On mount each tile of the grid fades in after a random delay, so the picture builds piecemeal, and the whole image starts greyscale. After a set pause the colours animate in together across every tile.
demo_content: A mountain range above a layer of cloud at sunset
search_phrases: photo breaks into squares that fade in
image assembles from a grid of tiles
mosaic load animation for a photo
picture builds itself tile by tile
use_when: A hero or gallery image should reveal itself with playful pixel drama instead of a plain fade.
avoid_when: Several images at once, since every tile loads and animates separately and the reveal gets slow.
customise: The image is src and the tile count comes from a preset grid name or a custom rows and columns object; fade time, stagger, colour delay and greyscale are props.
weight_why: A few dozen elements each fading one shared image with CSS opacity and filter.

a11y.note: Each tile has its own alt text, so a screen reader announces the same photo dozens of times.

issues: Every tile renders the whole image again, so the browser downloads and decodes the same photo many times.
polish_why: The tile reveal is satisfying and lands sharp; the mid-build gaps look broken for a beat.
